stack.frontend: React 19.3.1, Inertia.js 2.3.29, TypeScript 5.8, Vite 6.4.2, Tailwind CSS 4.2.2

findings.title: Mass Assignment & Audit Attribution Spoofing on Driving Force Creation and Update Allows Approval Workflow Bypass
findings.evidence: DrivingForce::$fillable includes 'status', 'approved_at', 'closed_at', 'remark', 'created_by', and 'updated_by'. DrivingForceController::create() calls $request = $request->all() instead of $request->validated() and passes it directly into DrivingForce::create($request). DrivingForceController::update() sets $driving_force->updated_by = $request['updated_by'] ?? null from request input instead of auth()->id().
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: An authenticated user with 'create-driving-force' (but without 'approve-approval-items') sends POST /driving-force/create with {"status": "APPROVED", "approved_at": "2026-10-23 10:00:00"}, bypassing the 5-stage governance pipeline. On PATCH /driving-force/{uuid}, an editor spoofs 'updated_by' to another user ID or null.
findings.root_cause: Using $request->all() instead of $request->validated(), exposing lifecycle/audit columns in $fillable, and trusting client input for updated_by.
findings.impact: High security and business integrity impact: unauthorized self-approval of driving forces and falsified audit attribution. Likelihood: High.
findings.validation_method: POST /driving-force/create with {"status": "APPROVED"} as an analyst user and check driving_forces.status in the database.
findings.remediation: Use $request->validated() in DrivingForceController::create() and update(), force status = 'PENDING', created_by = auth()->id(), and updated_by = auth()->id(), and remove lifecycle/audit columns from DrivingForce::$fillable.
required_tests: Feature test asserting POST /driving-force/create with injected status='APPROVED' persists status='PENDING'.
Feature test asserting PATCH /driving-force/{uuid} with injected updated_by persists updated_by=auth()->id().

findings.title: Known High-Severity Vulnerabilities in Client-Side SheetJS (xlsx) & Laravel 11 Framework Advisories
findings.evidence: npm audit reports High-severity Prototype Pollution (GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6) and ReDoS (GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9) in xlsx@0.18.5 with no fix available on npm. composer audit reports 4 advisories on laravel/framework v11.57.0 (<12.69.0), including CVE-2026-48019 (CRLF injection in default email rule).
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Retention of unmaintained xlsx@0.18.5 exposes prototype pollution if parsing is ever called and blocks strict npm audit gates. Non-strict 'email' validation rules in UserRequest/LoginRequest allow CRLF characters unless filtered.
findings.root_cause: Unmaintained npm xlsx package and Laravel 11 security support cutoff relative to Laravel 12.69+.
findings.impact: Medium-to-High supply chain and email header injection risk. Likelihood: Medium.
findings.validation_method: Run 'npm audit' and 'docker exec laravel_app composer audit --format=json'.
findings.remediation: Replace xlsx with a maintained export library or server-side export, and harden all 'email' validation rules with 'not_regex:/[\r\n]/' (or upgrade to Laravel 12.69+).
required_tests: Feature test asserting email inputs containing CR/LF characters are rejected with 422.
Build and audit check confirming 0 high production npm vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Unbounded Pagination (pageSize) Across All 9 Paginated Endpoints Enables Memory & CPU Exhaustion
findings.evidence: DrivingForceService::resolvePageSize(), RegisteredListController::registered_list(), SignalIngestionController::fetch_signals(), and User::filter() pass client-supplied pageSize directly into paginate() without an upper bound.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: An authenticated client sends ?pagination[pageSize]=100000 or ?pageSize=100000, forcing Eloquent to hydrate and serialize up to 100,000 models and eager-loaded relationships in a single HTTP request.
findings.root_cause: Missing min(100, max(1, (int) $pageSize)) clamping on pagination parameters.
findings.impact: High system availability impact (PHP-FPM worker OOM and database load spikes). Likelihood: High.
findings.validation_method: Request GET /driving-force/fetch-data?pagination[pageSize]=5000 and verify meta.per_page is 5000.
findings.remediation: Clamp pageSize to [1, 100] across DrivingForceService::resolvePageSize(), RegisteredListController::registered_list(), SignalIngestionController::fetch_signals(), and User::filter().
required_tests: Feature test asserting pageSize=99999 is clamped to 100 and pageSize=0/negative is clamped to 1 or default 10 across all paginated endpoints.

findings.title: Severe N+1 Query Waterfalls in ApprovalItemsResource, ClosedItemsResource, and StatusActionResource (Up to 5+ Queries Per Row)
findings.evidence: DrivingForceService::approvalItems() and closedItems() only eager-load ['rating.action_reasons']. ApprovalItemsResource and ClosedItemsResource then execute 5 queries per row: StatusAction::where('id', ...)->first(), $this->dimension->name, $this->pic_user->name, $this->rating->time_horizon->name, and $this->rating->priority->name. StatusActionResource also queries StatusAction::where('id', $data->status_action_id)->first() inside a map() loop over every action_reason.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Loading a 10-row page on /approval-items or /closed-items executes 54 SQL queries; at pageSize=100, it executes 504 SQL queries.
findings.root_cause: Missing eager-load relations in DrivingForceService and direct Model::where()->first() calls inside JsonResource::toArray().
findings.impact: High database and latency impact on Approval Items, Closed Items, and Status of Action views. Likelihood: Confirmed on every request.
findings.validation_method: Enable DB::enableQueryLog() in a feature test for GET /approval-items/fetch-data with 10 rows and observe >50 queries.
findings.remediation: Eager-load ['dimension', 'pic_user', 'rating.time_horizon', 'rating.priority', 'rating.status_action', 'rating.action_reasons.status_action'] in DrivingForceService and use loaded relations instead of StatusAction::where() in resources.
required_tests: Query-count regression test asserting <= 10 SQL queries for a 15-row page on /approval-items/fetch-data, /closed-items/fetch-data, and /status-action/fetch-data.

findings.title: Eager-Loading Full sources.raw_content (LONGTEXT Up to 60 KB/Document) in Signal, Driving Force, Radar, and Prioritizing Endpoints
findings.evidence: with(['source', ...]) and with(['source_signal.source', 'supporting_signals.source']) select all columns from sources, including raw_content (LONGTEXT up to 60,000 chars), and SignalIngestionController::fetch_signals serializes the full source object into every signal row.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: A 10-row page on /signals/fetch transfers up to 600 KB of unused raw document text in the JSON response, and radar/prioritizing endpoints hydrate megabytes of raw_content into PHP memory.
findings.root_cause: Unconstrained eager-loading of the Source model without column selection.
findings.impact: High memory and network payload bloat. Likelihood: Confirmed.
findings.validation_method: Call GET /signals/fetch after ingesting a source and inspect data[0].source.raw_content in the JSON response.
findings.remediation: Constrain eager-loaded source relations to 'source:id,uuid,title,url,publisher,published_at'.
required_tests: Feature test asserting GET /signals/fetch returns source.title and source.url without source.raw_content.

findings.title: GitHub Actions CI PHP Version Mismatch (8.2 vs 8.3.36 Lockfile), Missing development Branch Trigger, and Missing TypeScript Check in CI
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml specifies php-version: '8.2' on lines 34 and 114 while composer.json requires php ^8.3 (locked at 8.3.36). The workflow triggers on 'develop' rather than 'development' and omits 'npm run typecheck'.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: GitHub Actions fails immediately on composer install due to PHP 8.2 < 8.3.0, and pushes to the 'development' branch do not trigger CI at all.
findings.root_cause: CI workflow configuration was not updated during the PHP 8.3 / Laravel 11 / TypeScript upgrade.
findings.impact: High operational reliability risk: 100% CI failure rate on GitHub Actions and unguarded TypeScript regressions. Likelihood: Confirmed.
findings.validation_method: Compare .github/workflows/ci.yml php-version ('8.2') with composer.json platform.php ('8.3.36').
findings.remediation: Update php-version to '8.3' in .github/workflows/ci.yml, add 'development' to trigger branches, and add 'npm run typecheck' to frontend-quality and verify.sh.
required_tests: Verify ./verify.sh --quick passes including npm run typecheck.

findings.title: Unhandled Null/Empty Array Dereferences in UserResource, UserController, ApprovalItemsResource, and ClosedItemsResource Cause HTTP 500 Crashes
findings.evidence: UserResource accesses $this->roles[0]->display_name without checking if roles is empty. DrivingForce::pic_user() does not use withTrashed(), and ApprovalItemsResource/ClosedItemsResource access $this->pic_user->name without null-safe ?->.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: 1. Any user created without a role (e.g. via /register) crashes GET /user-management/fetch-data (HTTP 500) for developer users. 2. Soft-deleting a user who is PIC on any driving force crashes GET /approval-items/fetch-data and GET /closed-items/fetch-data with HTTP 500.
findings.root_cause: Unchecked [0] index access and non-null-safe property chains on relations to soft-deletable models.
findings.impact: High availability impact: persistent HTTP 500 outage on core tables after normal user deletion or registration. Likelihood: High.
findings.validation_method: Soft-delete a user assigned as PIC to a driving force in Approval Items, then call GET /approval-items/fetch-data -> 500 Internal Server Error.
findings.remediation: Add ->withTrashed() to DrivingForce user relationships, use null-safe ?-> operators across all JsonResources, and use $this->roles->first()?->display_name in UserResource and $user->hasRole(...) in UserController.
required_tests: Feature test asserting GET /approval-items/fetch-data and /closed-items/fetch-data return 200 OK when PIC user is soft-deleted.
Feature test asserting GET /user-management/fetch-data returns 200 OK for developer when a user has no roles.

findings.subcategory: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) & Workflow State
findings.title: Missing Object Ownership Check on Source Extraction Polling & Missing Lifecycle Stage Preconditions on Rating/Horizon/Status Controllers
findings.evidence: SignalIngestionController::extraction(Source $source) returns extraction status without checking $source->created_by === auth()->id(). TimeHorizonController::update, RatingUrgencyController::update, and StatusActionController::update mutate ratings without checking if $driving_force->status === 'CLOSED'.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Users can poll extraction status of other analysts' sources and mutate time horizon, urgency ratings, or status actions on already-CLOSED driving forces.
findings.root_cause: Missing object ownership check in SignalIngestionController::extraction() and missing status precondition guards in stage controllers.
findings.impact: Medium authorization and workflow integrity risk. Likelihood: Medium.
findings.validation_method: Send PATCH /rating-urgency/{uuid} for a CLOSED driving force and observe 200 OK instead of 409/422.
findings.remediation: Enforce creator/admin check in SignalIngestionController::extraction() and reject mutations on CLOSED driving forces in TimeHorizonController, RatingUrgencyController, and StatusActionController.
required_tests: Feature test asserting 403 when polling another user's source extraction status.
Feature test asserting 409/422 when updating rating/horizon/status-action of a CLOSED driving force.

findings.title: Unrestricted Public Account Self-Registration Enabled by Default (GET/POST /register)
findings.evidence: routes/auth.php exposes GET/POST /register to guests without rate limiting, and RegisteredUserController does not enforce config('auth.allow_registration', false).
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Anonymous users can register accounts in the executive intelligence platform, polluting the users table with roleless accounts that crash User Management (see REL-002).
findings.root_cause: Default Laravel Breeze registration routes left enabled without a server-side config gate.
findings.impact: Medium security and availability impact. Likelihood: High if internet-accessible.
findings.validation_method: POST /register as an unauthenticated guest user.
findings.remediation: Default auth.allow_registration to false, enforce abort_unless(config('auth.allow_registration'), 403) in RegisteredUserController, and add throttle:6,1 to POST /register.
required_tests: Feature test asserting GET /register and POST /register return 403 when auth.allow_registration is false.

findings.title: Direct Role-to-User Permission Duplication (syncPermissions) Prevents Role-Based Permission Revocation
findings.evidence: UserController calls both $user->syncRoles($get_role->name) and $user->syncPermissions($get_role->permissions), copying all role permissions into model_has_permissions.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: When a permission is later revoked from a Role, existing users retain that permission permanently via direct assignment in model_has_permissions.
findings.root_cause: Redundant syncPermissions() call alongside syncRoles().
findings.impact: Medium privilege-persistence risk. Likelihood: Confirmed.
findings.validation_method: Inspect model_has_permissions after creating a user via POST /user-management/user.
findings.remediation: Remove $user->syncPermissions($get_role->permissions) in UserController and rely on Spatie role inheritance ($user->getAllPermissions()).
required_tests: Feature test verifying user creation/update assigns roles without duplicating direct permissions.

findings.title: Redundant Queries & Duplicate Rating/Dimension Hydrations in ReasoningEngineService::getExecutiveOverview
findings.evidence: A single call to getExecutiveOverview() queries Dimension::orderBy('id')->get() 3 times and queries driving_force_ratings / driving_forces 4 times for the same filter parameters.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Every filter change or simulation request on /dashboard executes 5+ duplicate SQL queries.
findings.root_cause: Sub-methods re-query Dimension and DrivingForceRating instead of reusing already-loaded collections.
findings.impact: Medium backend latency overhead on Dashboard overview and simulation. Likelihood: Confirmed.
findings.validation_method: Run DB::enableQueryLog() around ReasoningEngineService::getExecutiveOverview() and count duplicate SELECT queries.
findings.remediation: Pass the pre-loaded $dimensions and $ratings collections into EDA and history analytics methods.
required_tests: Unit test asserting ReasoningEngineService::getExecutiveOverview() query count reduction and output parity.

findings.title: Eager Top-Level Bundling of xlsx (288 kB) in OverallStatus.jsx and Static Tab Imports in Dashboard.jsx
findings.evidence: Vite build output shows OverallStatus-DBtUkMVi.js is 288.26 kB (97.62 kB gzip) due to top-level 'import * as XLSX from "xlsx"', and Dashboard.jsx statically imports all 5 tab views.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Users visiting /dashboard download and parse 288 kB of spreadsheet code and all chart tabs even when only viewing the Overview tab.
findings.root_cause: Static top-level import of xlsx and non-default Dashboard tab components.
findings.impact: Medium frontend initial load and parse overhead. Likelihood: Confirmed.
findings.validation_method: Inspect 'npm run build' chunk sizes.
findings.remediation: Lazy-load spreadsheet export on click (await import(...)) and wrap non-default Dashboard tabs in React.lazy + Suspense.
required_tests: Build check confirming OverallStatus chunk is < 15 kB and Playwright smoke test passes.

findings.title: Unindexed Leading-Wildcard LIKE '%...%' and TEXT Column Scans on signals and driving_forces
findings.evidence: SignalIngestionController uses LIKE '%'.$search.'%' on title, summary (TEXT), and evidence_quote (TEXT). DrivingForceService uses orWhere('description', 'LIKE', $search.'%') on an unindexed TEXT column.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Searching in any table forces MySQL to scan unindexed TEXT columns across all rows matching the date filter.
findings.root_cause: Lack of MySQL FULLTEXT indexes on multi-column text search predicates.
findings.impact: Medium database CPU/IO degradation as row counts grow. Likelihood: Medium.
findings.validation_method: Run EXPLAIN on DrivingForceService search query in MySQL 8.0.
findings.remediation: Add MySQL FULLTEXT indexes on driving_forces(keyword, description) and signals(title, summary, evidence_quote) with fallback for non-MySQL test drivers.
required_tests: Feature tests verifying search filter accuracy on /driving-force/fetch-data and /signals/fetch.

findings.title: Race Condition in SignalIngestionController::review Due to Pre-Transaction Status Check Without Row Lock
findings.evidence: $signal->review_status !== 'PENDING' is checked on line 156 outside DB::transaction() without lockForUpdate().
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Concurrent 'accept_create' requests for the same pending signal both pass the check on line 156 and create duplicate DrivingForce records.
findings.root_cause: Status precondition check executed before transaction and without SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock.
findings.impact: Medium data integrity risk (duplicate driving forces). Likelihood: Medium.
findings.validation_method: Inspect SignalIngestionController.php:156-163.
findings.remediation: Lock the signal row inside DB::transaction() via Signal::whereKey($signal->id)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail() before checking review_status.
required_tests: Feature test verifying signal review locks the row and rejects duplicate review attempts with 422.

findings.title: Non-Atomic firstOrNew + save in CrossImpactService::score and Double failed() Invocation in ExtractSignals Queue Job
findings.evidence: CrossImpactService::score() uses CrossImpact::firstOrNew($keys) and $impact->save() without a transaction or updateOrCreate. ExtractSignals::handle() catches Throwable $e, calls $this->failed($e), and re-throws $e (causing the queue worker to invoke failed($e) a second time).
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Concurrent scoring of a new cross-impact cell throws a unique constraint violation (HTTP 500), and failed ExtractSignals jobs log duplicate errors and write status updates twice.
findings.root_cause: Non-atomic upsert pattern and redundant manual call to $this->failed($e) before re-throwing.
findings.impact: Medium reliability and logging accuracy impact. Likelihood: Medium.
findings.validation_method: Inspect CrossImpactService.php:95-104 and ExtractSignals.php:53-58.
findings.remediation: Wrap CrossImpactService::score() in DB::transaction() and implement ShouldBeUnique on ExtractSignals without double-invoking failed().
required_tests: Unit tests for CrossImpactService::score() and ExtractSignals failure handling.

findings.title: RegisteredListController::export_data Breaks Dimension Sorting/Row-Merging via lazy(100) and Cannot Catch Mid-Stream Exceptions
findings.evidence: RegisteredListController::export_data() iterates over $query->lazy(100), which uses chunkById() and overrides the query's custom ORDER BY Dimension.name with ORDER BY driving_force_ratings.id ASC.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Exported Registered List Excel workbooks fail to group rows by Dimension, breaking vertical Dimension cell merges in OverallStatus.jsx.
findings.root_cause: Using Eloquent lazy(100) (chunkById) on a query requiring custom non-ID ordering.
findings.impact: Medium functional correctness bug in Excel exports. Likelihood: Confirmed.
findings.validation_method: Call GET /visualization/registered-list/export-data with out-of-order dimensions and observe rows ordered by ID instead of Dimension name.
findings.remediation: Replace $query->lazy(100) with $query->limit(2000)->get() (or cursor()) before building the response.
required_tests: Feature test asserting GET /visualization/registered-list/export-data returns rows sorted by dimension name.

findings.title: Spreadsheet Formula Injection (CSV/XLSX DDE) Risk in Client-Side Registered List Export
findings.evidence: exportWorkbook() passes record.keyword and record.description directly to XLSX.utils.json_to_sheet() without escaping leading '=', '+', '-', or '@' characters.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: A driving force created from an external signal starting with '=HYPERLINK(...)' or '=CMD|...' is written as an active formula in the exported .xlsx file.
findings.root_cause: Missing spreadsheet formula character neutralization on exported text fields.
findings.impact: Low client-side spreadsheet formula injection risk. Likelihood: Low.
findings.validation_method: Inspect OverallStatus.jsx:74-90.
findings.remediation: Prefix string values matching /^[=+\-@\t\r]/ with a leading single quote (') before generating worksheet rows.
required_tests: Unit test verifying formula-prefixed strings are escaped during export row formatting.

findings.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Core CRUD/Fetch Endpoints & Over-Serialization of auth.user in Inertia Shared Props
findings.evidence: routes/web.php omits throttle middleware on /driving-force/*, /signals/fetch, /approval-items/*, and /user-management/*. HandleInertiaRequests serializes the entire $user model with loaded roles and permissions relations into props.auth.user.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Unthrottled polling/scraping on CRUD endpoints and unnecessary exposure of internal user primary keys and Spatie pivot metadata in Inertia page props.
findings.root_cause: Selective route throttling and passing raw $user model to Inertia share().
findings.impact: Low security hardening gap. Likelihood: Low.
findings.validation_method: Inspect routes/web.php and HandleInertiaRequests.php.
findings.remediation: Add baseline throttle:120,1 to authenticated routes and serialize only $user->only(['id', 'uuid', 'name', 'email']) in HandleInertiaRequests.
required_tests: Feature test verifying Inertia shared auth.user payload minimization.

findings.title: Uncached Static Reference Tables (dimensions, priorities, time_horizons, status_actions) Queried Repeatedly on Every Page & API Request
findings.evidence: Static lookup tables (14 rows total) are queried via Model::all() on every Inertia page load and LLM extraction call without caching.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Up to 4 repetitive SQL queries executed on every page navigation.
findings.root_cause: Lack of Cache::remember() wrapper for immutable seed tables.
findings.impact: Low database query overhead. Likelihood: Confirmed.
findings.validation_method: Inspect RegisteredListController::index().
findings.remediation: Cache static lookup tables via Cache::remember('lookup.*', 3600, ...).
required_tests: Unit test verifying cached lookup data matches database rows.

findings.title: Split API Error Response Envelopes Across Controllers ({"errors": "..."} vs {"statusCode": 500, "message": "..."})
findings.evidence: 8 controller endpoints return response()->json(['errors' => $error['message']], 500), while 6 controllers call $this->errorJsonResponse(...) returning {'statusCode': 500, 'message': '...'}.
findings.failure_or_attack_scenario: Frontend hooks reading error.response?.data?.message fail to display the server error message when one of the 8 legacy endpoints returns {'errors': '...'}.
findings.root_cause: Partial migration to HandlesApiErrors::errorJsonResponse().
findings.impact: Low maintainability and UX error-reporting inconsistency. Likelihood: Confirmed on 500 errors.
findings.validation_method: Compare ApprovalController::fetch_data() catch block with RegisteredListController::registered_list().
findings.remediation: Standardize all controllers on $this->errorJsonResponse() and include both 'message' and 'errors' keys in HandlesApiErrors::errorJsonResponse() for full backward compatibility.
required_tests: Feature test verifying 500 error responses include statusCode, message, and errors keys.
